purpose: Generator INTENT for the harness mirror fan-out, as data rather than as PowerShell. install.ps1 reads it to decide what to skip and where to degrade; the rt-observe collector reads the same file to decide whether an absent mirror is BY DESIGN or a LOSS. One truth, two consumers. Before this file existed, both facts lived inside install.ps1, which made the toolkit's own intent unreadable to anyone without PowerShell - which is most of the people who clone this repository.

provenance.inertness_proof: The generated trees were hashed before and after the extraction and compared file by file. The extraction is a move, never a change of value.
provenance.rule: A value here is the ONLY declaration of itself. install.ps1 must not restate one, and the two ceiling suites parse this file rather than the installer (R0, R2, R6).

copilot_stub_threshold.unit: characters of the canonical agent body
copilot_stub_threshold.provenance: chosen - a margin under copilot_hard_limit, so a body that grows between two installs does not cross the hard limit unnoticed
copilot_stub_threshold.effect: An agent body above this is replaced in .github/agents/ by a roughly 1700-character pointer stub. The agent's actual instructions then stop reaching GitHub Copilot while the install still exits 0, so the state is reported as 'stubbed' and never as 'ok'.
copilot_stub_threshold.measured_note: local-writer.md sat at 27544 body characters on 2026-08-28, a margin of 456. The next addition to that agent has to trim something first.

copilot_hard_limit.unit: characters of the GENERATED profile, frontmatter included
copilot_hard_limit.provenance: specified - GitHub Copilot's documented limit on a custom agent prompt
copilot_hard_limit.effect: install.ps1 throws rather than writing a profile above this. It is a hard stop, not a degradation.

codex_skill_list_budget.unit: characters of the concatenated skill list Codex assembles
codex_skill_list_budget.provenance: specified - Codex allots the skills list 2% of the model context window, or 8000 characters when that window is unknown. Verified 2026-08-28 against learn.chatgpt.com/docs/build-skills. This is the conservative case, not a constant of this repo, and a Codex user can raise it.
codex_skill_list_budget.effect: Over budget, Codex shortens descriptions itself and then omits skills with a warning. install.ps1 pre-empts that by trimming each description to whole sentences under a computed per-skill cap, so the state is 'trimmed' and never 'ok'. Adding a skill shrinks the cap for EVERY skill.
codex_skill_list_budget.measured_note: 15 skills produced 6198 of 8000 characters after trimming on 2026-08-30, with 11 of the 15 trimmed.

codex_doc_max_bytes.unit: bytes of the concatenated AGENTS.md chain
codex_doc_max_bytes.effect: Over the cap, Codex drops the DEEPEST file in the chain, which is the one closest to the work.
codex_doc_max_bytes.measured_note: The root plus .claude/skills/AGENTS.md chain was 5272 of 32768 bytes on 2026-08-30.

session_mode_commands.provenance: chosen - these four commands only change how a Claude Code session formats its output
session_mode_commands.reason: They have no meaning in another harness, so no prompt mirror is generated for them. An empty cell here is BY DESIGN and must never be reported as a loss. Conflating the two is the single defect the mirror matrix exists to prevent.

copilot-instructions.provenance: measured 2026-08-30 - .github/instructions/ holds six files where .claude/rules/ holds five
copilot-instructions.reason: mermaid.instructions.md is hand-maintained and has no source under .claude/rules/. Its own header says so. A mirror file with no canonical row is reported as 'orphan', and an orphan named here is deliberate rather than a leftover from a deleted rule.

vscode-user-instructions.provenance: measured 2026-08-30 - install.ps1 -Personal copies .github/instructions/*.instructions.md into the VS Code user profile, and that directory holds the hand-maintained mermaid file alongside the five generated ones
vscode-user-instructions.reason: Same deliberate orphan as the copilot-instructions column, arriving here because -Personal copies the whole generated directory rather than re-deriving it from .claude/rules/. Declared so the column reads by-design instead of accumulating one permanent orphan nobody intends to fix.

targets.note: Written ONLY under install.ps1 -Personal. Every agent added since the last -Personal run is therefore invisible to that harness, which is a real loss and not a design decision. Six agents were in that state on 2026-08-30. A user who has never run -Personal has no directory at all, which is reported as 'not installed' for the whole column rather than as 17 losses.

Copies the GENERATED prompt files into the VS Code user profile so they work in any workspace. It copies what .github/prompts/ holds, so the session-mode skip propagates here: those four were never generated, so they are by design absent from this column too. Same -Personal gate as the Copilot CLI column.

The same directory as the column above - VS Code keeps prompts and instructions together - but a different file suffix and a different source, so it is a separate column rather than one column with two templates. Modelling it as one produced a cell whose path was the directory itself, which existed for every name and therefore reported every rule as present.
Full body, no size ceiling, so this column has no 'stubbed' state.

BY DESIGN one pointer file rather than one mirror per rule. Continue receives a single rule that points at the canonical routing table. Four empty per-rule cells here are correct, and the column is scored as one cell, not five.
Created only when absent, so an operator's edits survive a regeneration. That also means a stale CONVENTIONS.md is never corrected by an install and must be reported as 'stale' rather than 'ok'.

Codex is the ONE harness with a native skill convention: it scans .agents/skills from the cwd up to the repository root and reads each SKILL.md for its name and description. The mirror is a frontmatter-only pointer whose description is trimmed to whole sentences, so a skill's trigger vocabulary must sit in its FIRST sentence, the one guaranteed to survive.
